title: Core ideas in astronomy
description: The scale and story of the universe, from the solar system to the Big Bang.

ideas.title: The solar system
ideas.summary: Eight planets orbit the Sun, held by its gravity, in a system about 4.6 billion years old.

items.q: About how old is the solar system?
items.a: About 4.6 billion years

items.q: In astronomy, what is an astronomical unit (AU)?
items.a: The average distance from Earth to the Sun, about 150 million km

items.q: About how long does light from the Sun take to reach Earth?
items.a: About 8 minutes

items.q: According to Kepler's first law, what shape is a planet's orbit around the Sun?
items.a: An ellipse, with the Sun at one focus

ideas.title: Earth, Moon and sky
ideas.summary: Seasons, phases and eclipses all follow from how the Earth and Moon move and tilt in the light of the Sun.

items.q: What causes the seasons on Earth?
items.a: The tilt of Earth's axis, about 23.5 degrees, and not its distance from the Sun

items.q: What causes the phases of the Moon?
items.a: As the Moon orbits Earth, we see different amounts of its sunlit half

items.q: How are the Sun, Moon and Earth arranged during a solar eclipse?
items.a: The Moon passes directly between the Sun and Earth

items.q: Which astronomer published, in 1543, the model in which Earth and the other planets orbit the Sun?
items.a: Nicolaus Copernicus

ideas.title: Stars
ideas.summary: A star is a ball of hot gas that shines by nuclear fusion, and its mass decides how it lives and how it ends.

items.q: What process powers the Sun and other stars like it?
items.a: Nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium in the core

items.q: What kind of dense remnant will the Sun leave behind after its red giant phase?
items.a: A white dwarf

items.q: What is the explosion that ends the life of a very massive star called?
items.a: A supernova

items.q: Where were elements such as carbon and oxygen originally made?
items.a: Inside stars, by nuclear fusion

ideas.title: Light and distance
ideas.summary: Nearly all we know of the sky comes from its light, and to look far away is to look back in time.

items.q: In astronomy, what is a light-year?
items.a: The distance light travels in one year, about 9.5 trillion km

items.q: Which star is nearest to the Sun, and about how far away is it?
items.a: Proxima Centauri, about 4.2 light-years away

items.q: Which technique spreads starlight into its colors to show what a star is made of?
items.a: Spectroscopy

items.q: In astronomy, what is redshift?
items.a: The stretching of light to longer wavelengths, as when its source is moving away from us

ideas.title: Galaxies and the expanding universe
ideas.summary: Stars gather in galaxies by the hundreds of billions, and the galaxies are moving apart as space expands.

items.q: What is the name of the galaxy that contains the Sun?
items.a: The Milky Way

items.q: Roughly how many stars does the Milky Way galaxy contain?
items.a: A few hundred billion (estimates run from 100 to 400 billion)

items.q: Which is the nearest large galaxy to the Milky Way, and about how far away is it?
items.a: The Andromeda galaxy, about 2.5 million light-years away

items.q: What did Edwin Hubble's observations of distant galaxies show in 1929?
items.a: The farther away a galaxy is, the faster it recedes from us, so the universe is expanding

ideas.title: The Big Bang
ideas.summary: The universe began hot and dense about 13.8 billion years ago and has been expanding and cooling ever since.

items.q: About how old is the universe?
items.a: About 13.8 billion years

items.q: What is the cosmic microwave background?
items.a: The faint afterglow of the hot early universe, released about 380,000 years after the Big Bang

items.q: What are the two most abundant elements in the universe?
items.a: Hydrogen and helium

items.q: What name is given to the unseen matter that astronomers infer from its gravitational pull on galaxies?
items.a: Dark matter
